title: A scanned Quick Connect QR opens the approval with the code filled in
description: TV apps draw a Quick Connect QR that links to <server>/web/#/quickconnect?code= (D-089).
notes: If the observation shows jellyfin-web already does criteria 2 and 3, the task closes on the capture and the docs line. Dropped (D-126 and the pivot, D-107): A Quick Connect QR for jellyfin-web (rule 3). Replaced by JS-191. Both auditors agreed.
acceptanceCriteria: Observed first, against Jellyfin 12.4 and jellyfin-web 12.4, recorded in compat/captures: what Moonfin 3.1.1's QR decodes to, and whether jellyfin-web's page at that address fills the code in, signed in and signed out.

A phone that scans Moonfin's QR, on a jellyscale serving jellyfin-web, reaches the approval with the code filled in. Signed out, it signs in by password or by the provider (JS-039) and returns to the approval with the code kept.
The approval names the device and app, and approves only on an explicit confirmation, never on opening the link.
The link carries Quick Connect's own code: one code, JS-037's expiry and guessing bound, no second pending-code flow, and no route that takes a code without a signed-in approver.
docs/status.md says which apps draw the QR and what a viewer does where no web client is served (type the digits).
If the observation shows jellyfin-web 12.4 does not fill the code in or loses it across sign-in, the lead returns with a brief before building. No file of jellyfin-web is changed.
